Rashi on Berakhot 8a:12:1.hebrew: לעת מצא זו מיתה - שימות במיתה יפה ונחה:
Rashi on Berakhot 8a:12:1.english: "At a time of finding," this is death - That he should die a good and peaceful death.

Rashi on Berakhot 8a:13:1.english: Askara [croup] - Estranglement [strangulation] in the vernacular [Old French], which is inside the body.

Rashi on Berakhot 8a:13:2.hebrew: כחיזרא בגבבא דעמרא דלאחורי נשרא - כענפי הסירים הנסבכים בגזת הצמר, כשאדם נותק בחזקה ומשליך לאחור, שאי אפשר שלא ינתק הצמר עמה:
Rashi on Berakhot 8a:13:2.english: Like a thorn branch in a bundle of wool that is pulled backward - Like the branches of thornbushes entangled in a fleece of wool, when a person tears [them] out forcefully and casts [them] backward, as it is impossible for the wool not to be torn out with them.

Rashi on Berakhot 8a:13:3.hebrew: כפיטורי בפי ושט - ים אוקיינוס יש בו מקומות שאינו מקבל ברזל, ומחברין לוחי הספינה ע"י חבלים ועקלים שתוחבי' בנקביו, ותוקעין אותו בדוחק, לפי שהם גסין כמדת הנקב:
Rashi on Berakhot 8a:13:3.english: Like ropes in the opening of the esophagus - In the ocean, there are places that do not accept iron, and they join the planks of the ship by means of ropes and cables that they thrust into its holes, and drive them in with difficulty, because they are thick, matching the size of the hole.

Rashi on Berakhot 8a:13:4.hebrew: פיטורי - חבלים, דמתרגמינן ופטורי ציצים (מלכים א ו׳:י״ח) אטונין:
Rashi on Berakhot 8a:13:4.english: Ropes - [Means] ropes, as we translate "and open flowers" (I Kings 6:18) [in the Targum as] "cords."

Rashi on Berakhot 8a:13:5.hebrew: בפי ושט - הוא הנקב, שהוא עגול כפי ושט:
Rashi on Berakhot 8a:13:5.english: In the opening of the esophagus - This is the hole, which is round like the opening of the esophagus.

Rashi on Berakhot 8a:13:6.hebrew: כמשחל בניתא מחלבא - כמושך נימת שער מתוך החלב:
Rashi on Berakhot 8a:13:6.english: Like drawing a hair from milk - Like one who draws a strand of hair out of milk.

Rashi on Berakhot 8a:14:1.hebrew: זיבולא בתרייתא שלמא - שיהא לו שלום כל ימי חייו, ואף ביום קבורתו עד השלכת עפר האחרונה שבכיסוי קבורתו:
Rashi on Berakhot 8a:14:1.english: The final shovelful, peace - That he should have peace all the days of his life, and even on the day of his burial until the final casting of earth in the covering of his grave.

Rashi on Berakhot 8a:14:2.english: Zivula [a shovelful] - Palade [shovelful] in the vernacular [Old French].

Rashi on Berakhot 8a:15:1.hebrew: לעת מצא זה בית הכסא - שיהא דר במקום שיש בית הכסא סמוך לו, לפי שהיתה קרקע של בבל מצולת מים, ואין יכולין לחפור שם חפירות, והיו צריכין לצאת בשדות ולהתרחק מאד:
Rashi on Berakhot 8a:15:1.english: "At a time of finding," this is a privy - That he should live in a place where there is a privy near him, because the land of Babylonia was a watery marsh, and they were unable to dig pits there, and they had to go out into the fields and distance themselves very far.

Rashi on Berakhot 8a:17:1.english: The distinguished [gates] - [This derives from the word] Zion; and [the dwellings of Jacob refer to] the assembly of the congregation.

Rashi on Berakhot 8a:1:1.hebrew: עת רצון - אלמא יש שעה שהיא של רצון:
Rashi on Berakhot 8a:1:1.english: A time of favor - Evidently, there is a time that is of favor.

Rashi on Berakhot 8a:20:1.hebrew: ביני עמודי - שבית המדרש נכון עליהם מלמעלה:
Rashi on Berakhot 8a:20:1.english: Between the pillars - That the study hall was supported upon them from above.

Rashi on Berakhot 8a:22:1.hebrew: שכל זמן ששמעי בן גרא קיים כו' - דסמוך למיתת שמעי, כתיב: ויתחתן שלמה את פרעה (מלכים א ג׳:א׳):
Rashi on Berakhot 8a:22:1.english: For as long as Shimi ben Gera was alive, etc. - For adjacent to the death of Shimi, it is written: "And Solomon allied himself by marriage with Pharaoh" (I Kings 3:1).

Rashi on Berakhot 8a:24:1.hebrew: הא דכייף ליה - אם כפוף הוא לרבו לקבל תוכחתו, ידור אצלו. ואם לאו, טוב להתרחק ממנו, ויהי שוגג ואל יהי מזיד:
Rashi on Berakhot 8a:24:1.english: This [is where] he submits to him - If he is submissive to his teacher to accept his rebuke, he should live near him. And if not, it is better to distance himself from him, so that he will be [acting] unwittingly and not be [acting] intentionally.

Rashi on Berakhot 8a:29:1.hebrew: מהדר אפיה וגריס - משנתו כשקורין בספר תורה:
Rashi on Berakhot 8a:29:1.english: Would turn his face and study - [He would study] his Mishnah while they were reading from the Torah scroll.

Rashi on Berakhot 8a:30:1.hebrew: ישלים פרשיותיו - של כל שבת ושבת:
Rashi on Berakhot 8a:30:1.english: [A person] should complete his portions - [The portion] of each and every Shabbat.

Rashi on Berakhot 8a:3:1.hebrew: כביר לא ימאס - תפלת הרבים לא ימאס:
Rashi on Berakhot 8a:3:1.english: Mighty, He will not despise - He will not despise the prayer of the multitude.

Rashi on Berakhot 8a:3:2.english: From the battle against me - From the battles that come upon me.

Rashi on Berakhot 8a:3:3.hebrew: כי ברבים היו עמדי - שהתפללו עמי:
Rashi on Berakhot 8a:3:3.english: For there were many with me - That they prayed with me.

Rashi on Berakhot 8a:4:1.hebrew: פדה בשלום - זה שעסק בדברי שלום, דהיינו תורה, דכתיב: וכל נתיבותיה שלום (משלי ג׳:י״ז). וכן גמילות חסדים נמי שלום הוא, שמתוך שגומל חסד בגופו לחבירו, הוא מכיר שהוא אוהבו, ובא לידי אחוה ושלום:
Rashi on Berakhot 8a:4:1.english: He has redeemed in peace - This refers to one who engaged in matters of peace, namely Torah, as it is written: "And all her paths are peace" (Proverbs 3:17). And so too, acts of kindness are also peace, for since he performs an act of kindness with his person for his fellow, [his fellow] recognizes that he loves him, and [this] leads to brotherhood and peace.

Rashi on Berakhot 8a:5:1.hebrew: הנני נותשם מעל אדמתם - סיפיה דקרא הוא:
Rashi on Berakhot 8a:5:1.english: Behold, I will pluck them up from off their land - This is the end of the [same] verse.

Rashi on Berakhot 8a:6:1.english: They go early - In the morning.

Rashi on Berakhot 8a:6:2.hebrew: מחשכי - ערבית, כלומר מאריכין בבית הכנסת:
Rashi on Berakhot 8a:6:2.english: Stay late - In the evening; that is, they prolong [their stay] in the synagogue.

Rashi on Berakhot 8a:8:1.hebrew: שיעור של שני פתחים - רוחב יכנס לפנים, שלא ישב סמוך לפתח, דנראה עליו כמשוי עכוב בית הכנסת, ויהא מזומן סמוך לפתח לצאת:
Rashi on Berakhot 8a:8:1.english: A distance of two doorways - [A distance of their] width he should enter inside, so that he does not sit near the doorway, for remaining in the synagogue would appear like a burden upon him, and he would be ready near the doorway to leave.

Rashi on Berakhot 8a:9:1.hebrew: יתפלל לעת מצא - יתפלל שיהו מצויין לו כשיצטרך:
Rashi on Berakhot 8a:9:1.english: Let him pray in the time of finding - He should pray that they will be available to him when he needs them.

Tosafot on Berakhot 8a:29:1.hebrew: רב ששת מהדר אפיה וגריס - וא"ת: והא אמרינן בסוטה (פ"ז ד' לט.), מאי דכתי' "וכפתחו עמדו כל העם" (נחמיה ח׳:ה׳) — כיון שנפתח ספר תורה אסור לספר, אפי' בדבר הלכה? ויש לומר: התם איירי בקול רם, כדי שלא יבטלו קול קריאת התורה; והכא איירי בנחת. והאי דקא מהדר אפיה — רבותא משמע: אע"ג דמהדר אפיה, שנראה כמניח ספר תורה, שפיר דמי; והאי דאהדר אפיה — כדי שיכוון גרסתו. ורב אלפס (מגילה פ"ד) כתב: דה"ג מפרשי, דוקא שיש שם עשרה אחריני אז יכול ללמוד; אבל אין שם עשרה כי אם עמו — לא. והכא מיירי שהיו שם עשרה בלא הוא. ועוד תירץ האלפסי: שאני רב ששת, שתורתו אומנתו הוא. ואנן מסתבר לן כי האי תירוצא:
Tosafot on Berakhot 8a:29:1.english: "Rav Sheshet would turn his face and study" - And if you say: But behold, we say in Sotah (ch. 7, 39a): What is [the meaning of] that which is written, "And when he opened it, all the people stood up" (Nehemiah 8:5)? Once the Torah scroll is opened, it is forbidden to converse, even regarding a matter of Halakhah! And one can say: There [in Sotah], it is dealing with [speaking] out loud, so that they do not disrupt the sound of the Torah reading; whereas here [with Rav Sheshet], it is dealing with [studying] softly. And this [detail] that he turned his face implies a novelty: even though he turns his face, so that he appears as one who abandons the Torah scroll, it is [nevertheless] permitted; and the reason he turned his face was in order to concentrate on his study. And Rav Alfas [the Rif] (Megillah ch. 4) wrote that the Halakhot Gedolot explains: Specifically when there are ten others [present], then he may study; but if there are not ten except with him, no [he may not]. And here, it is dealing with [a case where] there were ten [present] besides him. And the Alfasi further answered: Rav Sheshet is different, for his Torah was his profession. And to us, this answer seems reasonable.

Tosafot on Berakhot 8a:30:1.hebrew: שנים מקרא ואחד תרגום - יש מפרשים: והוא הדין ללועזות, בלע"ז שלהן הוי כמו תרגום שמפרש לפעמים. כי כמו שהתרגום מפרש לע"ה, כך הם מבינים מתוך הלע"ז. ולא נהירא, שהרי התרגום מפרש במה שאין ללמוד מן העברי, כדאשכחן בכמה דוכתי דאמר רב יוסף (מגילה ד' ג.): "אלמלא תרגומא דהאי קרא, לא ידענא מאי קאמר". ע"כ אין לומר בשום לשון פעם שלישית, כי אם בלשון תרגום:
Tosafot on Berakhot 8a:30:1.english: "Twice Scripture and once translation" - Some explain that the same applies to speakers of a foreign language: [reading] in their vernacular is like Targum, which explains [the text] at times. For just as the Targum explains [the text] to the common people, so too they understand from the vernacular. And this does not appear correct, for the Targum explains that which cannot be learned from the Hebrew [text], as we find in several places, where Rav Yosef said (Megillah 3a): "Were it not for the translation of this verse, I would not know what it is saying." Therefore, one should not recite [the portion] a third time in any language except in the language of the Targum.
